around.headline: Two Bengaluru traffic police personnel caught on camera accepting bribes
around.summary: Footage showing two traffic personnel taking cash from motorists has surfaced, renewing scrutiny of on-the-spot cash settlements for traffic violations. Many violations here are already camera-detected and auto-challaned to your vehicle, so paying cash on the spot doesn't cancel that record — always insist on a proper receipt or challan.

around.headline: Metro Blue Line trial run set for October, operations by 2027; fares to rise every 3 years
around.summary: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda has asked BMRCL to begin Blue Line trial runs in October ahead of a 2027 commercial launch, while a separate report says metro fares are now set to increase on a fixed three-year cycle. Regular metro commuters should budget for periodic fare hikes going forward.
around.source: The New Indian Express / Bangalore Mirror

around.headline: Revamp of Bengaluru Police Commissionerate on the cards
around.summary: Authorities are considering a structural overhaul of the city police commissionerate, though details of the changes are still emerging. Worth watching if you interact with your local police station, as jurisdictions or processes could shift.

around.headline: Karnataka to send delegation to brief PM Modi on drought conditions in the state
around.summary: Deputy CM D K Shivakumar said a delegation will apprise the PM of the state's drought situation, which typically also strains Bengaluru's water supply and vegetable prices given how much produce comes from rural Karnataka. Expect continued pressure on borewell levels and market prices for produce if the dry spell persists.

around.headline: Prahlad Joshi takes charge as Education Minister; PM Modi sets up task force on exam reforms
around.summary: Joshi has taken over from Dharmendra Pradhan, who resigned amid the exam paper-leak protests, and PM Modi has announced a task force on exam reforms led by an Infosys co-founder. Anyone tracking competitive-exam changes should follow this task force's recommendations over the coming weeks rather than today's protest headlines.

street_smart.title: A traffic constable pulls you over for jumping a signal and offers to 'settle it right now' for ₹200 cash instead of writing up a challan. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: two Bengaluru traffic police personnel were caught on camera accepting bribes from motorists (The Hindu), renewing scrutiny of on-the-spot cash settlements for traffic violations.
street_smart.situation: The constable waves you over, says he'll let the signal-jump slide for ₹200 cash right now instead of the usual fine, and is already gesturing for you to hand it over quickly since traffic is backing up behind you.

choices.text: Politely decline, ask for the official challan or e-challan receipt, and if he keeps pushing for cash, note his name/belt number and report it via the Bengaluru Traffic Police app, by calling 100, or to the Karnataka Lokayukta.
choices.feedback: Correct. Insisting on a paper trail is your strongest protection, and reporting a persistent bribe demand with the officer's name/badge number is exactly what leads to cases like today's, where two personnel were caught on camera doing this.

choices.text: Hand over the ₹200 cash on the spot since it's less hassle than dealing with a challan.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A large share of Bengaluru's traffic violations are now camera-detected and auto-challaned straight to your vehicle's registered owner regardless of what happens on the road — so the cash doesn't cancel that record. You could end up paying twice, and you've also just committed bribery yourself, which is an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

choices.text: Refuse to engage at all and just drive off without stopping.
choices.feedback: Driving off from a legitimate traffic stop can be treated as evading a lawful order and may get your vehicle flagged. Don't ignore the stop — just insist on proper documentation instead of cash.

choices.text: Pay the cash but ask the constable to write you a quick handwritten note as 'proof' of payment.
choices.feedback: A handwritten note from the same person demanding the bribe isn't a valid receipt and won't protect you from a separate e-challan later, or from the officer denying it ever happened. Only an official challan number counts.

takeaways: A large share of Bengaluru's traffic violations are already camera-detected and auto-challaned — paying a bribe on the spot doesn't cancel that electronic record.
Report bribe demands by traffic police via the Bengaluru Traffic Police app, by calling 100, or through the Karnataka Lokayukta (anti-corruption ombudsman).
A cop who refuses to give you a proper receipt or challan number and insists only on cash is the clearest sign of a bribe attempt, not a legitimate fine.

quiz.q: Under India's Prevention of Corruption Act, who can be held liable in a bribery transaction?
options: Both the giver and the taker of the bribe
Only the government official who takes it
Only the person who offers it
Neither, if the amount is under ₹500
quiz.why: This is why 'just paying the cop' isn't a legally safe shortcut — offering a bribe is itself an offence, not just accepting one.
